intent: Let the laptop reach the phone over adb at any time without anyone opening Settings, tapping a pairing dialog, or reading a port off the screen.
scope: Non-goal: no change to deploy.sh, which already assumes port 5555
Non-goal: no router DHCP reservation - MAC discovery replaces the need for one
changes: Wait for any transient Wireless debugging window (trying a known port first, then an nmap sweep of the ephemeral range), then use it to setprop service.adb.tcp.port=5555 and restart adbd.
Install a Magisk service.d boot script that re-applies the port on every boot, so the phone comes back reachable without interaction.

Find the phone by MAC when the configured IP is wrong: the phone is on DHCP with no reservation, so a hardcoded address is a latent failure. A ping sweep populates the neighbour table and the MAC is looked up there.

Match the exact ip:port when deciding whether a connection exists. The first version took the first `device` line, and since pairing also leaves an mDNS _adb-tls-connect._tcp entry for the same phone, it reported port 5555 as reachable while nmap showed it closed.

verification.evidence: Installed the boot script (-rwxr-xr-x root root 373) and switched the port; nmap -p 5555 then showed '5555/tcp open' where it had shown 'closed' immediately before.
'phone moved: 192.168.1.99 -> 192.168.1.64' then 'reachable on 5555 at the new address'. MAC discovery works.

verification.command: adb reboot; ./enable_persistent_adb.sh   # no arguments, no interaction
verification.evidence: 'already reachable on 5555 - nothing to do'. /proc/uptime was 149s so the reboot was real, and getprop service.adb.tcp.port returned 5555, proving the boot script ran rather than a stale adbd surviving.

verification.command: Observed port drift during one session
verification.evidence: Wireless debugging offered 35545, then 40401, then 43781, and the listener vanished entirely twice when the screen slept. This is the failure mode the fixed port removes.

risks: adbd on a fixed port is reachable to anything on the LAN. It still requires an authorised key and an unknown key prompts on-device, but this is a wider surface than ephemeral Wireless debugging. Accepted explicitly by the user.
PHONE_MAC is hardcoded to this handset; a new phone needs that constant updated. The script would otherwise silently fail to rediscover a moved device.

Credential-encrypted storage means a freshly rebooted, still-locked phone accepts adb but cannot screencap or read app data until it is unlocked once - relevant when scripting post-reboot verification.
rollback: rm /data/adb/service.d/99-adb-tcp-5555.sh and reboot, or setprop service.adb.tcp.port -1 followed by stop/start adbd to drop back to USB-only.
Confirm with nmap -p 5555 that the port is closed afterwards, and that Wireless debugging still works as the bootstrap path.
